text.p: Bangladesh on Tuesday appointed one minister, three state ministers and two deputy ministers, officials said.
The appointments expanded the cabinet of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to 31 ministers.

Newly-appointed Syeda Sajeda Chowdhury was named Minister of Environment and Forest. A senior member of the ruling Awami League, she lost in the June 12 election but was named an MP from the reserve parliamentary seats for women.

The state ministers are M. Amanullah, who was assigned to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Talukder Abdul Khaleque, to the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief, and Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, to the Ministry of Planning.
The new deputy ministers, Dhirendra Debnath Shambhu and Jinnatunnesa Talukder, were assigned to the Ministry of Shipping and the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education, respectively.
President Shahabuddin Ahmed administered the oath of office to the new ministers.
Alamgir is a career bureaucrat and had been secretary to Hasina until Tuesday.
State Minister for Law and Parliamentary Affairs Abdul Matin Khasru was promoted to the rank of full minister and given the same portfolio, the officials said.
